title: Ordinary nonreducedness spreads from the generic fibre
statement: Let $h:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $T$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point]. If the scheme-theoretic fibre $Z_\xi$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is not reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], then there is a nonempty open subset $W\subseteq T$ such that $Z_t$ is not reduced for every $t\in W$. No flatness, Noetherianity, or reducedness of $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: First replace $T$ by $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $Z$ by $Z\times_TT_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] the new base is reduced and has the same topological space, hence is irreducible and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The residue fields are unchanged: on an affine chart the quotient by the nilradical induces $(A/\sqrt{0})_{\mathfrak p/\sqrt{0}}/(\mathfrak p/\sqrt{0})=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p$. Thus the old and new fibres are canonically isomorphic by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Local finite type and quasi-compactness persist by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], so the new morphism is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A nonempty open found on this new base therefore gives the required open on the old base. In the remaining steps $T$ is integral.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, first four sentences: reduction of the base

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $T$. It contains $\xi$, and $A$ is a domain with fraction field $K=\kappa(\xi)$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] and [def-weil-residue-field]. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $h^{-1}(T_0)$ has a finite affine open cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with each $B_i$ finite type over $A$. Their generic fibres are open and cover $Z_\xi$, using [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]; they are $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i\otimes_AK)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Since $Z_\xi$ is not reduced, [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-open-cover] gives an index $i$ whose generic fibre is not reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], its ring has a nonzero nilpotent element. Fix this chart, writing $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $0\ne e\in B\otimes_AK$ with $e^n=0$, $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, affine reduction and selection of a nonzero nilpotent generic section

proof.text: Write $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. The generic ring is $S^{-1}B$: the mutually inverse maps are $b\otimes(a/s)\mapsto ab/s$ and $b/s\mapsto b\otimes(1/s)$, as follows from the tensor relations and the fraction relation in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] at $(0)$. Express $e=b/s$. The equation $e^n=0$ means that some $0\ne a\in A$ has $ab^n=0$ in $B$. Over $D(a)$ put $h=b/1\in B_a$. Then $h^n=0$, while $h$ remains nonzero in the generic ring because $e\ne0$ and $s$ is invertible there. Replace $A,B,T_0,U$ by $A_a,B_a,D(a),U\times_{T_0}D(a)$. Here $D(a)$ contains $(0)$, and the localized algebra is still generated by the original finite list [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Thus $h\in B$ is now nilpotent and generically nonzero. This writes out both denominator shrinkings in the source.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, spreading and making the section nilpotent

proof.text: Set $I=\operatorname{Ann}_B(h)=\{b\in B:hb=0\}$, $C=B/I$, and $D=B/hB$. These are finite type $A$-algebras: the images of generators of $B$ generate each quotient [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Multiplication by $h$ gives the short exact sequence $0\to C\xrightarrow{\iota}B\to D\to0$, with $\iota(\bar b)=hb$: the kernel of multiplication is exactly $I$, and its image is $hB$. Moreover no nonzero scalar $a\in A$ lies in $I$, since $ah=0$ would make $h=0$ in the generic ring, where $a$ is invertible. In particular $C$ and every localization $C_a$ for $a\ne0$ are nonzero: $1=0$ in $C_a$ would say that some power of $a$ belongs to $I$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, annihilator quotient and its generically nonzero fibre

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial algebra $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ surjecting onto $B$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Both $C$ and $D$ are cyclic, hence finite, $P$-modules. Apply [lem-pur-generic-finite-module-presentation] first to $(A,P,C)$ and then to $(A,P,D)$, obtaining $a_C,a_D\ne0$. Restrict to $A_a$ for $a=a_Ca_D$; then $C_a,D_a$ are finitely presented over $P_a=A_a[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. To check persistence on this common restriction, localize each finite presentation: a fraction in the kernel has a numerator whose image is killed by a power of the inverted scalar, so after multiplying that numerator by the power it lies in the original image; this proves exactness of the localized presentation. The identity $P_a=A_a[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ sends a polynomial with coefficient fractions to a common-denominator polynomial and has the coefficientwise inverse. This uses precisely the finite-presentation part of generic flatness, with no Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, generic flatness, finite-presentation preparation of C and B/hB (Tag 051T)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-fp-algebra-module-generic-freeness] over the domain $A_a$ to the finitely presented algebra $P_a=A_a[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ (zero relations) and each of the finitely presented modules $C_a,D_a$ of step 5. After two further principal restrictions, both are free over the same localized base. Indeed further localization of a free module preserves its basis: localize the unique finite coefficient expansion of each element [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. e0$. This obtains the source's nonzero free $C$ and flat quotient, even making the quotient free.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, generic flatness for C and B/hB, using Tag 051S after the Tag 051T preparation

proof.text: Fix any $t\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ and put $k=\kappa(t)$. Since $D$ is free, it is flat in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: tensoring an injection with a module with basis $J$ is the direct sum of copies of that injection indexed by $J$, hence is injective, by the finite-support coefficient expansion [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-module-base-change]. The basis of $C$ has a member since $C\ne0$. Its coordinate inclusion $A\to C$ has a retraction $C\to A$, so after tensoring with $k$ it exhibits $k$ as a retract of $C\otimes_Ak$; hence $C\otimes_Ak\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to the short exact sequence of step 4 and $N=k$. Thus $C\otimes_Ak\to B\otimes_Ak$, $\bar b\otimes\lambda\mapsto hb\otimes\lambda$, is injective. Its source is nonzero, so it is a nonzero map. If $h\otimes1$ were zero, every displayed image would be $(h\otimes1)(b\otimes\lambda)=0$, a contradiction. Therefore $h\otimes1$ is a nonzero nilpotent, its $n$th power being zero.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, tensoring the short exact sequence with residue fields (Tag 00HL)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the ring in step 7 is the coordinate ring of $U_t$. Hence $U_t$ is not reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. It is an open subscheme of $Z_t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]; if $Z_t$ were reduced its local rings, and therefore those of this open, would be reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Thus every fibre over the final principal open is nonreduced. Every scalar inverted was nonzero in a domain, so that open contains $\xi$ and is nonempty; it is open in $T_0$, hence in the integral base. Step 1 identifies it with a nonempty open $W$ in the original $T$ and identifies its fibres with the original fibres, completing the claim.
